evaluations.label: A
errors: Action Items section says '(none)' although Andre committed to find out about separating rooms and Susan committed to ask Maggie and Pierrette

'noting this is common in other faculties but not necessarily here' inverts the transcript: sharing with assistants is a tradition at the school, while other faculties give professors their own offices

Uses generic 'Speaker 1/2/3/4' labels that do not match the transcript's speaker letters, so attributions (e.g. 'Speaker 4 expressed a preference for sharing rooms with assistants') cannot be traced and are effectively wrong
'Members were tasked with consulting colleagues, such as Maggie and Pierrette' - Susan volunteered to ask them; it was not a general task
Lounge described as 'a significant requirement... to serve as a meeting or overflow space' - its purpose was explicitly left open
'Unimile building' - transcript says Unimail
'negotiation with other groups in the building' - there is one other group
strengths: Correct core numbers (15 people, ~18 positions including reading room)
Lists the open questions (partitioning, four in a three-person room, lounge purpose) clearly
Next meeting Tuesday 2 PM stated correctly
weaknesses: Summary and outline largely duplicate each other
Misses that number of rooms is fixed but assignments are open, the growth concern, and the Gisella/school-admin idea

evaluations.label: B
errors: 'Andrei' and 'UniMile' are misspellings of Andre and Unimail (minor)
'Susan and Martin both raised concerns about sharing offices' slightly overstates Martin, who said he had nothing against sharing (though the next sub-bullet corrects this)
strengths: Clearly states what is fixed (room count) vs open (assignments) and that no layout was decided
Captures key numbers: 16 slots for 15 people if reading room uses a two-person room, zero growth, one free visitor slot
Action items have correct owners (Andre: room separation; Susan: Maggie and Pierrette)
weaknesses: Action items omit Andre checking four places in a three-person room and asking about Gisella sharing with school admin
Everyone's task to bring a sketch/proposal is in the body but not in action items
Meeting time stated as 'discussed' rather than agreed; MDM morning conflict not mentioned
Omits the idea of placing Gisella with other school admin

evaluations.label: C
errors: Action item assigns 'Follow up with absent team members (Maggie, Pierrette)' to Andrei; Susan volunteered to do this
'Distribute documents of the new office configuration' listed as an action item, but it happened during the meeting
'Management recognizes this as a priority due to previously lengthy discussions on its value' is not supported
'Lounge Priority: A lounge/reading room is key' overstates it; its purpose and need were questioned and left open
'desk arrangements inside rooms can be flexible' - what is flexible is which people go in which rooms
'merge proposals with another group before next Tuesday's review meeting' - merging comes after the proposals, not before Tuesday
'Smoking is allowed only outside, even on balconies' is garbled
'The session will focus on refining the plan rather than final decisions' is not supported
Many timestamps are wrong (e.g. 00:06 for the space overview, 19:34 for building-permission topics)
strengths: Covers almost every topic, including the four-in-three-person-room idea, the Gisella/school-admin idea, coffee and cafeteria hours
Notes that the number of rooms is fixed and the other group's role
weaknesses: Very long and repetitive; the same points (growth, room splitting, visitors) recur in several sections
Wrong owner on a key action item
Hard for a reader to pick out what was actually decided

evaluations.label: D
errors: 'Majority lean toward a mixed-use room' - Martin said some people want a mixed room and that no decision was taken; no majority was shown
'Strong support for a dedicated lounge' slightly overstates; Susan asked whether it was needed
'Unimile' is a misspelling of Unimail (minor)
strengths: Concise, well organized and accurate on numbers (18 positions, 16 slots for 15 people, zero growth)
Captures all next steps: room separation, four desks in a three-person room, Gisella with school admin, Maggie and Pierrette, draft proposals, Tuesday ~2 PM after the MDM meeting
Good coverage of Gisella options, project grouping rejected, smoking no longer a constraint, coffee details
Correctly notes professor-assistant sharing is a tradition that cannot be imposed
weaknesses: Next steps have no owners (Andre investigating, Susan asking Maggie and Pierrette)
Does not explicitly say the number of rooms is fixed while assignments are open

rationale: D is the most complete and readable, accurately covering every next step and the key constraints, though it omits owners. B is the most precise and correctly assigns owners but leaves out several next steps. C covers a lot but is repetitive, contains invented claims and gives the Maggie/Pierrette task to the wrong person. A lists no action items, uses speaker labels that cannot be traced, and gets the point about other faculties backwards.
